proof:
Put $K_\delta=\{(z,q):(z,\delta q)\in K\}$. Its tangential projection lies in the fixed compact projection $D$ of $K$ and its normal projection lies in $Q$. For every $q\in Q\setminus\{0\}$ write $q=s w$ with $s>0$ and $(a,w)\in K$. Convexity shows that the section of $K_\delta$ at $q$ contains $(1-\delta s)F+\delta s a$ when $\delta s\le1$; at $q=0$ use $F$. Thus it contains each prescribed compact subset of $\operatorname{relint} F$ for sufficiently small $\delta$, by its positive interior margin (with the singleton convention in dimension zero). A compact subset of $\operatorname{int}Q$ lies in the convex hull of finitely many points of $\operatorname{int}Q$, for example vertices of a finite collection of small boxes there. Applying the preceding section inclusion at these vertices and using convexity gives uniform inner inclusion on every interior product compact, in particular a fixed source ball about $(x,v)$. Conversely, at bounded $|q|$ the tangential coordinates in $K_\delta$ approach $F$ uniformly: any contrary subsequence has a limit $(z,0)\in K$ with $z\notin F$. This proves local almost-everywhere convergence of the indicators to $F\times Q$ on $D\times Q$. The excluded boundaries have measure zero, omitting the tangential boundary when $m=0$.

The source ball bounds the optimizing parameters by testing denominator positivity in the opposite parameter direction. The compact denominator floor is $1/(d+1)$ on $K_\delta$. A uniform objective upper bound follows by testing $1+t\ell\cdot(q-v)$ with $\ell\in\operatorname{int}Q^*$ and $t>0$ small: it is bounded below by a positive multiple of $1+|q|$ on $D\times Q$, and $d+1>k$. For any convergent parameter subsequence, the floor passes to $F\times Q$, first on its interior by inner inclusion and then by continuity. Fatou gives an integral there at most the limit inferior, finite along any convergent energy subsequence. This parameter is admissible in the exact product theorem, which gives the required lower bound.

For recovery test the fixed product optimizer. At bounded $|q|$, the uniform tangential approach to $F$ and $b_*\cdot q\ge0$ give a uniform positive lower bound on $K_\delta$. At large $|q|$, strict positivity of $b_*$ on cone unit vectors dominates all bounded tangential terms over $D$. Thus the test is admissible for small $\delta$ and has integrable majorant $C_1(1+|q|)^{-d-1}$ on $D\times Q$. Dominated convergence gives the matching product value. Product uniqueness then identifies every parameter cluster point. Undoing normal dilation contributes exactly $\delta^k$.

By convergence, the optimizing normal vectors stay in a compact subset of $\operatorname{int}Q^*$. The same large-$|q|$ estimate and the compact floor bound the normalized escorts by $C_2(1+|q|)^{-d-2}$ on $D\times Q$. This is integrable with weight $1+|q|$ in dimension $k$. Dominated convergence proves the dilated convergence, including moments; the original normal variable is $\delta q$, giving the undilated weak limit. The product law identifies the marginal and conditional mean. For a polytope, its projected cone is finitely generated by projected vertices; a face-exposing normal is strictly positive on each nonzero generator after choosing its sign. This proves closedness and pointedness.

statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^k$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with exposed face $K\cap(\mathbb R^m\times\{0\})=F\times\{0\}$ of dimension $m$, and let $Q=\operatorname{cone}(\pi K)$ be closed and pointed for projection onto the normal coordinates. Here $k\ge1$ and $\operatorname{cone}(\pi K)=\{s q:s\ge0,\ q\in\pi K\}$. Fix $x\in\operatorname{relint} F$, $v\in\operatorname{int} Q$. Use the point-face convention of singleton counting measure if $m=0$. Write $d=m+k$, $C=(m!/d!)(d+1)^{d+1}J_*(v)/[k^k(m+1)^{m+1}]$, and $L_F=1+a_F\cdot(z-x)$ for the optimal tangential energy denominator. Then $(x,\delta v)\in\operatorname{int}K$ for small $\delta>0$, and
$$
\delta^{-k}E_K(x,\delta v)\longrightarrow C E_F(x),\qquad
(c_\delta,\delta b_\delta)\longrightarrow
(c_*,b_*)=\left(\frac{m+1}{d+1}a_F,\frac{k}{d+1}n_v\right)
$$
for the original optimum $1+c_\delta\cdot(z-x)+b_\delta\cdot(q-\delta v)$. Under normal dilation by $\delta^{-1}$, its escort density converges in $L^1$ and in first moments to the product escort with denominator $L_*=(m+1)L_F/(d+1)+b_*\cdot q$ and normalization $CE_F(x)$. The undilated laws converge weakly to the tangential escort on $F\times\{0\}$; in the dilated limit the conditional normal mean is $L_F(z)v$. Every face of a full-dimensional polytope has the stated projected-cone property in these coordinates.
title: Projective energy and escorts at an actual pointed exposed face
